Evidence/CLM-006
Evidence record

Finance severity within a specific denominator

What does this evidence establish?

Among the formal firms in the report's finance-obstacle tabulation, which excludes firms that said they did not need a loan, the shares rating finance as a major or a moderate obstacle together total 91.84%.

What does it measure?

The combined share of formal firms rating access to finance as a major or moderate obstacle, among firms in the survey report's finance-obstacle tabulation (firms that said they did not need a loan are excluded), seven governorates, 2022.

Who or what does it apply to?

Formal enterprises in seven selected governorates

When was it measured or observed?

September 2022

How current is it?

The latest observation in this record refers to the 2022 survey (September 2022). It should not be read as describing a later period unless a newer comparable observation is published.

What this evidence does not establish

The combined 91.84% is not the share of all Yemeni firms that face a major or moderate finance obstacle; it applies only to the firms in the report's filtered tabulation.

Limits of the measure

The survey is not national, and the finance-obstacle table uses a filtered base whose number of firms is not recorded in the evidence base; some other tables rest on small conditional bases.

Method and verification detailDetail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Two shares reported by the source for the 2022 World Bank custom enterprise survey (September 2022), in Yemen Financial Sector Diagnostics (2024), Annex III, Figure 107 ('Degree by Which Access to Finance is an Obstacle'), p. 145; the source's tabulation excludes firms that said they did not need a loan. The combined 91.84% is computed by this resource as the sum of the two shares: major obstacle 68.71% plus moderate obstacle 23.13%.
